newsitem.title: CANADA: Ethyl to claim at least $200 mln from Canada.
newsitem.headline: Ethyl to claim at least $200 mln from Canada.

text.p: Ethyl Corp said on Thursday that it will claim at least US$200 million, possibly more, in damages from the Canadian government as a result of its ban on the fuel additive MMT.
"It's going to be higher," Ethyl official Jeff Polowin told Reuters. "Not like double or anything, but higher."
Earlier on Thursday the Virginia-based company said it would make good its threat to seek compensation from the Canadian government for the impact of the MMT ban imposed by Canada.

The Canadian Senate on Wednesday passed a bill which will ban the import and interprovincial trade of methylcyclopentadienyl mangananese tricarbonyl. Ethyl Corp's Canadian subsidiary supplies the Canadian market with the additive and effectively loses its main market with the passage of the bill.
The claim will be filed within the next few days and Ethyl said it expects a ruling later this year.
A company spokesman, Chris Hicks, said Ethyl had hired an international accounting firm to calculate damages caused by the Canadian ban.
Ethyl Corp said it will file a claim for compensation under the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA).
